comments.off: Comments are turned off for this account.
comments.failed: The comments could not be loaded.
comments.refreshFailed: The comments could not be refreshed. The list below is the last one loaded.
comments.hint: Plain text. A person you name is told, if they can see this item.
comments.mentionHint: Type at least two letters, then choose a person. Their name is added to the text.
comments.tooLong: A comment may be at most {max} characters.
comments.tooLines: A comment may have at most {max} lines.
comments.tooMentions: A comment may name at most {max} people.
comments.saveFailed: The comment was not saved. Your text is still here.
comments.role: Your role on this item does not allow this.
comments.limit: This item has as many comments as it can hold. Nothing was saved.
comments.notAuthor: Only the person who wrote a comment can change its text.
comments.replyToReply: A reply goes under a top-level comment, not under another reply. The list has been refreshed.
comments.rateLimited: Too many changes in a minute. Wait a minute, then try again.
comments.peopleRateLimited: Too many searches in a minute. Wait a minute, then try again.
comments.confirmDeleteBody: The text is removed for everyone. Its replies stay.
activity.empty: Nothing has been recorded for this item yet.
activity.failed: The activity could not be loaded.
viewers.note: A convenience, not evidence. It lists each person's last view in the last 30 days, while the view is still in their Recent list. Someone who clears Recent leaves the list. A view through a link or a token is not listed. The list does not show whether anyone read the file.
viewers.empty: No one has viewed this item in the last 30 days.
viewers.failed: The list could not be loaded.
settings.comments: Allow comments on files and folders
settings.commentsHint: When this is off, nobody in the account can read or write comments. The comments are kept, and they come back when it is turned on.
settings.whoViewedHint: Off by default. When it is on, a manager of a file can see who viewed it in the last 30 days. Views are listed from the time this is turned on. Turning it off hides the list, and turning it on again starts a new period. The list is a convenience, not evidence.
